A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 30 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A and B, support reliable comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v3 reports original evaluations of four VLM decoders, including benchmark performance, modality contributions, and explanation self-consistency in Section 4 and Appendices B.5–B.6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–3, uncertainty analyses, and individual examples in Tables 4–11.

M1.justification: The decoder extension of MM-SHAP, contribution normalization and aggregation, CC-SHAP procedure, and edit-based tests are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use VQA, GQA, GQA balanced, MSCOCO, FoilIt, and the same VALSE instruments, retaining the same generation and multiple-choice tasks.

E2.justification: The four evaluated VLM decoders, seven unimodal/encoder comparators in Figure 1, and six edit-based tests are unchanged. Figure 1 revises score assignments without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B.4 retain the same model sizes, prompts, metric definitions, full-VALSE performance evaluation, and 100-sample SHAP/self-consistency evaluations. Figure 1's reassignment does not document a protocol change.

E4.justification: The post-hoc versus CoT comparisons, task-specific analyses, and individual-instance studies in Appendix B.6 and Tables 4–11 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix B.5 and Figures 7–8 retain standard deviations over three runs for existence and VQA. Statistical reporting in the tables is also unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1 changes the reported percentage pairs (acc, acc_r): LXMERT (60,54) to (54,60), ViLBERT (64,51) to (51,64), ViLBERT 12-in-1 (75,63) to (63,75), and VisualBERT (46,49) to (49,46). GPT1's 61, GPT2's 60, and CLIP's 64 switch from acc to acc_r. Decoder scores and Tables 1–11 remain unchanged; these are revised metric assignments, not demonstrated performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the Shapley-value definitions, properties, approximation, and CC-SHAP formulation in Appendices B.1–B.2 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and findings: extending MM-SHAP to decoders, evaluating self-consistency, benchmarking VALSE, and finding stronger image contributions during explanation generation.

C2.justification: The limitations summary in Section 5 removes the explicit qualification that the evaluated VLMs are designed for English. That applicability boundary is not relocated to Appendix A. Other limitations and result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Hardware, computation times, FlashAttention-2 and quantization details, model links, and prompts remain unchanged. The existing code URL moves from the abstract to a footnote without changing access information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference entries, and stated novelty relative to previous MM-SHAP and CC-SHAP research are unchanged. Bibliographic movement across pages is layout reflow.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header, briefly rewrites the limitations and acknowledgements, and restores a bullet for LLaVA-NeXT-Vicuna. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with revised bar colors and positions for the metric assignments and adjusted proportions. Moving the code link to a footnote and compacting text cause limited page reflow; other figures and tables retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The main experiments and appendices remain unchanged. Figure 1 may correct an acc/acc_r assignment error, but neither PDF explains the reassignment or supplies independent baseline results that establish which version is correct. Minor presentation refinements coexist with removal of the explicit English-language limitation, so the supplied evidence does not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
